definition: Impeccable means so flawless as to be beyond criticism.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word impeccable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know impeccable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Strangers assumed the thrift-store suit was bespoke; her tailoring was that impeccable.
Presentable merely clears the lowest bar — fit to be seen, no more; impeccable sits at the other end of the scale, where even a hostile eye finds nothing to hold.
Polished work has been buffed until it shines, yet a sharp eye can still find the smudge; impeccable goes further and leaves the sharp eye nothing at all.

Flawless reports an inspection of the thing itself: not one defect anywhere in it. Impeccable makes the further boast — so flawless that criticism is left with nothing to say, no toehold for even a hostile judge. A gem can be flawless in fact; impeccable manners defeat the fault-finders.

Faultless is the plain zero-defect finding — nothing to fix, nothing to apologize for — and it stops at that arithmetic. Impeccable carries the same zero with a flourish: it pictures the sternest critic circling the work and walking away empty-handed. Faultless counts; impeccable defies you to count.

The tabloid dug through the senator's whole career and came back with nothing but peccadilloes.
Impeccable means so flawless as to be beyond criticism.
Odile's manners were impeccable in four languages.
She never reached across a table, never interrupted, never let a name slip her mind twice; her thank-you notes were postmarked before her hosts had finished the dishes.
Diplomats' wives studied her; one swore she had once watched Odile turn down a live eel, at a state dinner, in a way that flattered the chef.
Impeccable is the exact word because Odile's manners are so flawless as to be beyond criticism — not merely good, but offering criticism no toehold at all.
The word admits no degrees.
Polished manners can survive a lapse; impeccable ones, by definition, haven't had one.
Save it for the performance that gives even an unfriendly eye nothing to hold.
Impeccable is a finding of zero: no fault found, none findable — reserve it for the one performance in a hundred that survives unfriendly inspection.
This unit's meticulous describes the worker's care; impeccable describes the finished work's state.
A meticulous tailor may still deliver a crooked seam; when the seam offers criticism nothing to hold, the suit is impeccable.

The championship ended on a disputed goal, and within an hour both clubs had filed formal complaints against the rookie referee, Dana Okafor.
Each side hired its own analyst, certain that a frame-by-frame review would turn up the call that had robbed them.
The league replayed all ninety minutes twice.
Every offside flag matched the line; every card matched the rulebook's own examples; the disputed goal stood on three camera angles.
The final report used a word the league office rarely risks: Okafor's officiating had been impeccable.
Two clubs looking for blood had, between them, found nothing to cite.
Both complaints were withdrawn the same week, and Okafor was assigned the season opener.
